reviews.title: Deactivated my business number days into a paid subscription — no refund, no explanation
reviews.text:
I subscribed to Line2 for an iPhone business line, expecting a reliable number I could use for client communications. Instead, just a few days into my paid subscription, Line2 deactivated my business number without warning. This was not a minor inconvenience — this was the phone number I had already started giving to new business contacts and prospects.

When I contacted support, they refused to provide a refund and would not even tell me why my number was deactivated. That is completely unacceptable for a paid business communications app. If a company is going to remove access to a customer’s paid business line, the absolute minimum standard should be a clear explanation and a refund for service they failed to provide.

Because of Line2’s actions, I lost access to several new business contacts and likely lost sales. Prospects who had my new number could no longer reach me, and I had no way to recover those missed opportunities. For any business owner, freelancer, or professional relying on a second line, that kind of failure can directly harm your reputation and revenue.

I would strongly warn anyone considering Line2 for business use: do not trust this app with an important phone number. A business phone line needs to be stable, transparent, and backed by accountable support. My experience was the opposite — unreliable service, no explanation, no refund, and real damage to my business.

reviews.title: Constant Problems
reviews.text:
I’m leaving a negative review because of ongoing reliability issues and the way support handled them.

I rely on this number for business communication, and I recently experienced a serious problem where SMS messages sent from my Line2 VoIP number were not being received by Spectrum and Verizon customers. That is a major issue when texting is part of daily operations.

Support responded by saying the problem could not be replicated when they tested on three carriers and suggested that I contact the receiving carriers myself. That is not a reasonable resolution. My service relationship is with Line2 as the VoIP provider. When messages originating from the platform are not being delivered, I expect the provider to investigate the deliverability issue rather than directing customers to troubleshoot with large carrier networks.

During troubleshooting I also learned that an app update required the app to be deleted and reinstalled for things to function properly. That is important information that should be communicated proactively. There was no notice in the app or guidance from support suggesting that step, and customers should not have to guess that reinstalling the app is required after an update.

Unfortunately this is not the first time I have experienced reliability problems with Line2. Between the recurring messaging issues and the lack of a meaningful resolution from support, I no longer have confidence in the platform for business communication. As a result, I plan to move my number away from Line2 to another provider.

For a service that businesses depend on for calls and messaging, reliability and accountability matter. My experience here has not reflected that.

UPDATE

After my original review, the developer responded asking me to submit another support request and move the conversation off the App Store using a support code. It’s not difficult to understand why companies do this. Moving the conversation off the review page keeps the full sequence of events from remaining visible to other users.

The issue is that I had already gone through support.

Around February 2025, when Line2 implemented the required 10DLC registration, I completed the process as instructed. Something on Line2’s side then caused my number to lose the ability to make outbound calls for nearly a month before it was eventually corrected.

In March 2026 I contacted support again because SMS messages from my number were not being received by Spectrum and Verizon customers.

The response I received was:

“The line was tested on three separate carriers and the issue was not replicated. That means the issue is not with your Line2 service; it’s with the carrier that is receiving the message.”

So the issue was dismissed and attributed to the receiving carrier.

After submitting negative feedback and requesting the information needed to port my number to another provider, the situation escalated. Support began asking to troubleshoot again and I then received a notice stating my account had been flagged for business-related SMS messaging and that SMS on my number may be suspended.

So the sequence was:

I report an SMS delivery problem.
Support says there is no issue with their service.
I submit negative feedback and request port-out information.
My account is then flagged and I’m warned SMS may be suspended.

For a service marketed as a business phone platform, that experience speaks for itself.

reviews.title: Use google voice instead.
reviews.text:
Used their services for around 8 years. Not the best, but it did what we needed for a business line (had to forward to LAN for calls to be clear and not drop). 

More recently though, they pushed some nonsense about having to register and it costing extra. They were not able to answer properly and support is worse than a chatbot. They said it was necessary so that our texts weren’t blocked by carriers.. this would not have been the case. Instead of letting us continue, THEY blocked us from being able to text. Nothing to do with carriers or anybody else.

We ported the number and without any warning, they immediately closed the account and deleted all of our saved messages, voicemails, etc. This was a business line. Didn’t even have the decency to refund the other half of the month that was already paid for on top of that. We assumed we would still be able to access our info as we tested the waters. Nope.  The bozo from support acted like they were personally offended that we switched by their wording.

Do yourself a favor. Use google voice. I regret not starting with that in the first place. To say I’m disappointed after so many years of service is an understatement. I wouldn’t use or recommend their services even if they paid me.
A month? You’re crazy

reviews.title: Can’t text; lacks basic software functionality.
reviews.text:
If you plan to use Line2 for business—AVOID! 

They block texting until you complete an overly complex DLC registration, requiring you to dissect every word, update your website, and navigate red tape. 

Other services make registration fast; my colleague showed me his completed his DLC registration that took 1 day. My business line2 has been blocked for MONTHS from sending texts despite multiple attempts updating my privacy policy, website, etc. 

Line 2’s failure to resolve basic compliance issues and lack of simple features (like longer text support, cannot send multiple pictures) makes this a hard NO. 

They excel at billing, but they haven’t invested enough in their infrastructure to consistently deliver long-term value.
